subsystems.name: Body and limbs
subsystems.role: a human-shaped structure so it can use tools and spaces built for people.
parts: joints with harmonic or cycloidal drives

subsystems.name: Actuators
subsystems.role: convert electricity into the high torque needed to lift, walk and grip.

subsystems.name: Hands
subsystems.role: the hardest part — manipulation rather than locomotion.

subsystems.name: Perception
subsystems.role: sees and feels the world well enough to act in it.

subsystems.name: Control and balance
subsystems.role: keeps a two-legged machine upright while it works.

subsystems.name: Policy model and compute
subsystems.role: the 'brain' that turns what it sees and is told into motor commands.

subsystems.name: Fleet learning loop
subsystems.role: every robot's experience improves every other robot.

buildSteps.title: Design for human spaces
buildSteps.detail: Set reach, height and payload from the tools and doorways it must handle, then size joint torques backwards from that.

buildSteps.title: Build actuators
buildSteps.detail: Motor, gearbox and encoder are assembled into sealed joint modules, tested for torque, backlash and heat.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the body
buildSteps.detail: Limbs and torso are built from lightweight metal or composite, with cabling routed to survive continuous flexing.

buildSteps.title: Fit hands and sensing
buildSteps.detail: Fingers, tactile pads, cameras and force sensors are installed and calibrated.

buildSteps.title: Wire compute and power
buildSteps.detail: An onboard computer runs perception and control; a battery pack sets runtime — usually a few hours.

buildSteps.title: Learn to move in simulation
buildSteps.detail: Physics simulation trains locomotion and balance policies, which are then transferred to hardware.

buildSteps.title: Collect real demonstrations
buildSteps.detail: Human operators teleoperate the robot through tasks so the exact motion and outcome are recorded.

buildSteps.title: Train the policy
buildSteps.detail: Vision-language-action models are trained to map camera images plus a spoken or written instruction to actions, then fine-tuned on the robot.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Robots run a narrow job under supervision; failures and corrections feed back into the next model.

prerequisites.why: small, light, strong joints decide whether a robot can lift real loads without overheating.
general manipulation needs the sense of touch, which remains far behind vision.
demonstrations show instructions plus images driving actions, but reliability is still low.
training in simulation is cheap, but the gap to messy reality is still large.

prerequisites.tech: Robot safety standards for shared workplaces
prerequisites.why: rules mostly assume caged industrial arms, not free-roaming machines next to people.
sufficient onboard computing and batteries exist, though runtime is a limit.

pathway.milestone: humanoids from several companies walk in labs and pilot factories; Atlas, Optimus, Figure and 1X machines are all real programs
pathway.unlocks: proof that the mechanics and control can work at human scale.

pathway.milestone: single-task reliability in structured settings such as warehouses and assembly lines
pathway.unlocks: commercial deployment where the environment is known and variants are few.

pathway.milestone: general-purpose robots handling varied manual tasks with supervision
pathway.unlocks: work across construction, agriculture, care and logistics.
broad substitution of manual labour — which raises questions of cost, safety and economic disruption as much as engineering ones.
